identity.name: Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate
alt_names: Colony and Protectorate of Sierra Leone

land.text: the Freetown peninsula, the Sierra Leone Company's colony taken over by the Crown in 1808

predecessors.note: The af-04-a dossier freetown-colony runs 1787-1808 and names british-colonial-empire as its successor; this dossier carries the same land on from 1808.

capitals.name: Freetown
capitals.note: 'Freetown served as the capital of British West Africa through the entity's entire existence'; the Colony page names Freetown the capital.

correction.text: the Freetown peninsula (the Western Area), the Crown colony before the protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Colony page gives no area and no frontier for the Crown colony; the History page names no 19th-century cession (Sherbro, Bullom, the Banana Islands and Bonthe are absent from it), so only the peninsula the pages connect to Freetown is drawn. The Freetown dossier's Cliopatria 1796 shape (3,430 km2) is larger than the Western Area (about 560 km2); a gap-filler with a page on the colony's 19th-century cessions should widen this.

correction.text: the Colony and the Protectorate together, the territory of modern Sierra Leone

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 31 August 1896: 'the hinterland of Sierra Leone became a British protectorate'; the Protectorate page says it 'included the interior' of present-day Sierra Leone and its boundaries were demarcated with French Guinea and Liberia (no dates on the pages). The modern country stands for colony plus protectorate; the 1895 Paris line with French Guinea is 'roughly fixing the line' only.

ledger.note: 1808: 'It took responsibility of Sierra Leone in 1808 and made it a Crown colony.' The Protectorate page: the Crown colony 'was established in 1808'. The Freetown dossier (af-04-a) ends the Sierra Leone Company's colony in the same year.

region.text: the interior of Sierra Leone outside the Freetown peninsula, declared the Sierra Leone Protectorate

ledger.note: 31 August 1896: 'the hinterland of Sierra Leone became a British protectorate' (History page: 'a Proclamation was issued in the Colony declaring that territory to be a British Protectorate'). The land is the interior of modern Sierra Leone; the pages name no chiefdom and no area. Counterpart given as a string: the hinterland chiefdoms (History page: the 1890-1891 treaties were 'cooperative agreements between two sovereign powers', not cessions).
27 April 1961: 'Sierra Leone gained independence from the United Kingdom on 27 April 1961' (granted in a ceremony in Freetown; on 4 May 1960 the UK had agreed to the date).

wars.name: Hut Tax War of 1898
belligerents: Temne, Loko and Mende rebels under Bai Bureh and Momoh Jah
wars.outcome: British victory. Northern revolt (Temne and Loko under Bai Bureh) from February 1898, Bai Bureh surrendered 11 November 1898; the Mende rising in the south-east began later in 1898 and 'British forces under Lieutenant-Colonel J. W. A. Marshall defeated most of the rebels within two months'. It 'ended large-scale organised armed opposition to colonialism in Sierra Leone'.
wars.note: The page names no battle sites and no territorial change; no zone is drawn.

certainty.note: No frontier on any page; the peninsula only.
Modern country stands for the protectorate; boundary dates with France and Liberia are not on the pages.

notes: Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate has no Cliopatria row (the Freetown Colony row ends 1796; the sierra-leone row starts 1961). Four pages. The pages are thin on land: none gives an area, a list of 19th-century cessions or a date for the Liberian boundary, so the 1808-1895 shape is only the Freetown peninsula and the 1896 gain is the rest of modern Sierra Leone as one block. Not shown: the Colony's membership of British West Africa (17 October 1821, with the Gold Coast and Gambia settlements; dissolved 13 January 1850, reconstituted 19 February 1866, ended 28 November 1888) is an administrative union and has no event here. The 1895 Paris line with French Guinea and the 1895 Order-in-Council are described but give no land transfer; the French Guinea side would be a gain/loss against a French dossier (af-08). Bonthe and Sherbro were never opened. Gazetteer: the Freetown peninsula is the Natural Earth admin-1 'Western' of Sierra Leone (alias Western Area).
